beforeCard.prompt: Над какой полярной областью каждую весну наблюдают озоновую дыру?

answers.note: Над Арктикой тоже бывает сильное истощение озона, но ежегодную озоновую дыру связывают прежде всего с Антарктикой.
Антарктическая озоновая дыра сезонно развивается в южнополярной стратосфере.
Гренландия лежит в Арктике, но не является центром ежегодной антарктической озоновой дыры.
Аляска находится в высоких северных широтах, далеко от области антарктической озоновой дыры.

beforeCard.explanation: Это Антарктика. Весной Южного полушария очень холодный полярный вихрь создаёт условия для быстрого разрушения стратосферного озона.

finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: NASA L22,L27 locates seasonal ozone hole over Antarctica; NOAA Q11 L452-L457 distinguishes it from Arctic depletion. All options are genuine polar places; only Antarctica answers the question.

finalGroupBindings.literal: Это Антарктика. Весной Южного полушария очень холодный полярный вихрь создаёт условия для быстрого разрушения стратосферного озона.
finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: NASA L22 places the event in Southern Hemisphere spring; L33-L39 connects winter cold, polar vortex/PSC chemistry, sunlight return and ozone destruction.

finalGroupBindings.literal: Над Арктикой тоже бывает сильное истощение озона, но ежегодную озоновую дыру связывают прежде всего с Антарктикой.
finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: NOAA Q11 L453-L456 says Arctic depletion occurs in most years but is less severe/more variable; L469-L474 records rare strong episodes. The note’s distinction is accurate.

authorAssessment.grammar: Each answer follows the preposition “над” as a grammatically valid named polar location; all four options are parallel geographic targets.
authorAssessment.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: The Arctic is a credible distractor because it does experience significant ozone depletion in most years, and some winters (including 1997, 2011 and 2020) had unusually strong depletion. It is still wrong for the full prompt: NOAA says this Arctic loss is less severe/more variable and that an extensive recurrent ozone hole as in Antarctica does not occur there; NASA places the seasonal hole over Antarctica. The note is useful because it acknowledges real Arctic loss while preserving the defining annual Antarctic contrast.

authorAssessment.grammar: Each answer follows the preposition “над” as a grammatically valid named polar location; all four options are parallel geographic targets.
authorAssessment.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: “Над Антарктикой” is the only choice matching the whole question: NASA locates the exceptionally depleted ozone-hole region over Antarctica and dates its seasonal occurrence to the start of Southern Hemisphere spring (August–October). The note is truthful and useful because it adds NASA’s operational boundary of total column ozone at or below 220 Dobson Units, a measurable fact absent from the prompt/key.

authorAssessment.grammar: Each answer follows the preposition “над” as a grammatically valid named polar location; all four options are parallel geographic targets.
authorAssessment.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: Greenland is a plausible polar distractor because NOAA PMEL includes all of Greenland within the Arctic, which the prompt asks about broadly. It is wrong because the ozone hole in the prompt is the seasonal Antarctic region: NASA locates that region over Antarctica, not Greenland; NOAA distinguishes recurrent Antarctic ozone hole conditions from Arctic depletion. The note is true and useful: Greenland belongs to the Arctic, but is not the center of the Antarctic ozone hole.
